reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5, curriculum and design work delegated by George
factChecks: Independently recomputed all 120 numeric keys from first principles in packages/curriculum/tests/engineering-content.test.ts: 60 lesson and practice answers, 24 recall answers and 36 course-check answers. The test spells out every unit conversion (kN to N, GPa to MPa, 10⁶ mm⁴ to m⁴, rpm to rad/s) and checks the I-section by the parallel-axis theorem rather than the subtraction used in the prompt. Rounded keys (8.66 kN, 20.98 × 10⁶ mm⁴, 3,141.6 W, 1,885 W) sit within their stated tolerances.

The engine's own invariants are tested separately in packages/activity-engine/tests/engineering.test.ts: beam reactions satisfy ΣF = 0 and ΣM = 0, end moments vanish, dM/dx equals V numerically, the largest moment sits at zero shear; every truss joint balances in x and y; ideal pulleys and gear trains conserve work and power; meshing wheels share pitch-line speed.

Reviewed all 48 teaching beats and their 98 cases for given values that would leak a beat's answer. Changed four before publication: the balanced seesaw case (it stated the 1.5 m answer), the closing 10 kN force, a 480 mm² bar and a gear-direction question whose playback would show the answer. Explorer drawings hide reactions, member senses, stresses, deflections, effort and output speeds until the learner has answered.

Checked definitions and standard relationships against OpenStax University Physics Volume 1 sections 10.3, 10.6, 10.8, 12.1–12.4 and College Physics 2e sections 7.7 and 9.5, Engineering Statics: Open and Interactive sections 4.1, 5.3, 6.4, 8.4 and 10.2, and MIT OCW 2.001 (Fall 2006) lectures 20–22. Licence pages were read on 6 October 2026: all four are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so every source is recorded as reference-only. All prose, problems, drawings and the cover are original.

Writing and curriculum validation report no issues: 72 lesson questions, 5 multiple choice (7%), 7 one-word answers, every numeric question with a three-step hint ladder that does not state its answer.

Started a local stack with a disposable database and the mock tutor, and inspected screenshots of the course page, every explorer kind, answered states and all twelve placement visuals at 1440×900 and several at 390×844. Fixed label collisions, gradient strokes that vanished on horizontal members, filter regions that clipped rotated gears on phones and CSS variables missing from check visuals. Finite playback, reduced motion and keyboard controls are covered by component tests; the browser e2e spec is written but was not run by the author.
Editorial review is by the authoring agent under delegated authority. There has been no independent human subject review and no documented learner trial.
changes: Added a twelve-lesson course in four modules: loads and equilibrium, structures, beams and stiffness, and machines. 72 questions, 24 recall cards and 48 answered visual beats.
Added twelve-item placement, mixed checkpoint and seven-day delayed application checks with engineering check visuals.

Added the engineering explorer: ten bounded model kinds (forces at a point, moments, beams with shear and moment diagrams, trusses solved by joints, tensile tests, bending of sections, cantilever deflection, levers, pulleys and gear trains) with finite playback, keyboard controls and reduced motion.
